label: Living in Berlin
lede: I write these for people who already live here, not for people passing through. Every guide starts from a Berlin date, a Berlin price or a Berlin rule that just moved, and ends with the one thing I would actually do about it.
shelfLegend: By the part of life it hits
shelfLegendSub: Four shelves, because that is how the questions actually arrive

lead.title: Kältehilfe Berlin: What to Do When Someone Is Sleeping Out in the Cold
lead.excerpt: The Berliner Kältehilfe runs from 1 October to 30 April, with about 1,000 emergency places in the coldest months. Here is which number answers at which hour, why October is the gap month before the buses start, where the shelters are, and what to give.
lead.alt: A snowy street at Breitenbachplatz in Berlin at night, with falling snow lit by the street lamps and the elevated motorway bridge in the background
lead.line: is when the Kältehilfetelefon stops answering in October, and the Kältebus and the Wärmebus only start on 1 November.

glossary.gloss: The certificate that unlocks subsidised flats. The Wohnungsamt takes off an employee allowance and up to thirty percent before it compares anything, and Berlin issues five of them rather than one, which is why most people rule themselves out against the wrong number.

glossary.title: Berlin Election: Which Ballot Your Passport Gets You
